newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends down in light pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends down in light pre-holiday trade.

text.p: COMEX copper ended weaker in light, pre-holiday trading with end of week profit-taking and easing spreads on LME dampening prices, traders said.
Trading was relatively quiet as COMEX closed an hour early ahead of the President's Day weekend in the U.S. The exchange is closed on Monday.
The cash to three months premium or backwardation on LME dipped $15 to $20 Friday to $80/$85.
LME stocks rose in line with trader expectations, up 3,250 tonnes to 221,725 tonnes.
March COMEX settled 0.35 cent weaker at 107.70 cents per pound, traded 108.20 to 106.50 cents. March settled 0.55 cent up on the week.
In a report released on Friday, Bloomsbury Minerals Economics said the world's copper market was already in substantial surplus but this was obscured by government stockpiling.

Cumulative stock increases could be 600,000 tonnes over the 1996-1999 period, but if the Chinese continue to buy off LME to replenish stocks, it may discourage speculators selling the market short, Bloomsbury said.
But Richard de J Osborne, ASARCO's chairman, president and chief executive reitereated his view to reporters and analysts Friday that the copper market will remain in deficit this year and next.

"There are no big, hidden hoards of copper," Osborne said. Traditionally, after a steep backwardation eased, metal that was put in exchange warehouses is taken back by consumers and producers, and Osborne expected this to happen again.
Last year ASARCO forecast a surplus of 65,000 tonnes in Western World copper markets for 1997, but has since revised its outlook to a 17,000 tonne deficit.
